original_question: Find the asymptotic value of DhatSigma(n), where DhatSigma(n) is the minimum, over all planar n-point sets P, of the sum over p in P of the number of distinct distances from p to the rest of P.
target_in_paper: Section 9 ("Additional problems"), Problem 37 in the current arXiv version of arXiv:1406.1949: determine the asymptotic value of \hat D_\Sigma(n). This is the same quantity that appears as Problem 35 in the June 2014 draft PDF of the survey.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right extremal quantity, the minimization over all planar n-point sets, the fact that the objective is a sum of per-point distinct-distance counts, and that the paper asks for its asymptotic order.
missing_details: The paper's exact notation is \hat D_p(P), \hat D_\Sigma(P), and \hat D_\Sigma(n), not just an informal 'DhatSigma(n)'.
The ambient space is the Euclidean plane: P is a finite set of n distinct points in \mathbb{R}^2, and distances are ordinary Euclidean distances |pq|.
For each p \in P, the local quantity is defined explicitly by \hat D_p(P)=|\{\,|pq| : q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}|.
The summed quantity is \hat D_\Sigma(P)=\sum_{p\in P}\hat D_p(P); a distance value may contribute separately for different base points p.
The extremal function is \hat D_\Sigma(n)=\min_{|P|=n}\hat D_\Sigma(P), where the minimum ranges over all n-point planar sets with no extra restrictions such as general position or convexity.
To make 'asymptotic value' stand alone, one should say this means determining the order of growth of \hat D_\Sigma(n) as n\to\infty, up to constant factors.

The nearby context in the paper records the benchmark upper bound coming from a \sqrt n\times\sqrt n integer lattice, namely \hat D_\Sigma(P)=\Theta(n^2/\sqrt{\log n}), and states that Erdős conjectured this to be tight; that conjectural target is part of the paper's intent.
The problem is presented immediately after the single-point extremal function \hat D(n); that nearby context explains the currently stated lower-bound route via Katz and Tardos.
refined_question: For a finite set P\subset\mathbb{R}^2 and a point p\in P, let \hat D_p(P):=|\{\,|pq|:q\in P\setminus\{p\}\,\}| be the number of distinct Euclidean distances from p to the other points of P. Define \hat D_\Sigma(P):=\sum_{p\in P}\hat D_p(P), and let \hat D_\Sigma(n):=\min_{|P|=n}\hat D_\Sigma(P), where the minimum is over all n-point sets P\subset\mathbb{R}^2. Determine the asymptotic order of \hat D_\Sigma(n) as n\to\infty; in particular, is the integer-lattice upper bound \hat D_\Sigma(n)=O(n^2/\sqrt{\log n}) tight, i.e. does one have \hat D_\Sigma(n)=\Theta(n^2/\sqrt{\log n})?
justification: This is the exact problem targeted by your draft. In Section 9 the paper first defines the local count \hat D_p(P), then the sum \hat D_\Sigma(P), then the extremal function \hat D_\Sigma(n), and immediately states the open problem 'Find the asymptotic value of \hat D_\Sigma(n).' The same paragraph also gives the intended benchmark: a \sqrt n\times\sqrt n integer lattice yields \hat D_\Sigma(P)=\Theta(n^2/\sqrt{\log n}), and Erdős conjectured that this upper bound is best possible. So the sharp stand-alone version should keep exactly this extremal Euclidean-plane problem, with the paper's notation and lattice benchmark, and should not broaden it to other distance notions or additional geometric restrictions.
